title: U.S. House · Maryland's 1st District
area: Maryland's Eastern Shore and part of northeastern Maryland, including Cambridge, Salisbury, Bel Air and Ocean City.

context.text: Andrew Harris defeated Christopher Bruneau 79.7%-20.3% in the June 23, 2026 Republican primary. Dan Schwartz defeated Randi White, Victor Guidice and George Walish in the Democratic primary with 46.3% of the vote.

summary.text: Andrew Harris is the Republican incumbent seeking re-election in Maryland's 1st Congressional District. A physician and Naval Reserve medical officer, he served 12 years in the Maryland State Senate before his election to Congress in 2010. He chairs the House Freedom Caucus and sits on the House Appropriations Committee.

background.text: Born January 25, 1957, in Brooklyn, New York, the son of immigrants from Eastern Europe, according to his official biography.
Earned a B.S. (1977) and M.D. (1980) from Johns Hopkins University and an M.H.S. from Johns Hopkins in 1995.
Worked as a physician at the Johns Hopkins Hospital for nearly three decades, specializing as an anesthesiologist in obstetric anesthesiology.

Joined the U.S. Naval Reserve in 1988 as a medical officer, established and commanded the Johns Hopkins Medical Naval Reserve Unit, and was called to active duty in 1990 for Operation Desert Shield and Desert Storm at Bethesda Naval Hospital. He reached the rank of Commander and left the Reserves after seventeen years.
Elected to the Maryland State Senate in 1998 and served 12 years; Wikipedia lists him as minority whip from 2003 to 2006.
First elected to the U.S. House in 2010 and has represented Maryland's 1st District since January 2011.

Serves on the House Appropriations Committee, chairing its Subcommittee on Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies and serving on the Labor, Health and Human Services, Education subcommittee.
Elected chairman of the House Freedom Caucus on September 17, 2024; he is an original member of the group.

According to his official biography, he was married to his late wife, Cookie, for over 33 years, has five children, one stepchild and ten grandchildren, and lives in Dorchester County with his wife Nicole.

priorities.text: Health care, describing himself as keenly aware, as a physician, of the challenges Americans face accessing care.
Agriculture, saying he continues in Congress the work he did promoting and protecting Maryland agriculture and poultry as a state senator.
Immigration enforcement, saying porous borders and visa overstays undermine the American workforce and create national security risks.

positions.summary: Says illegal immigration undermines the American workforce and creates national security risks, and supports enforcement against undocumented immigrants and visa overstays.
Says local governments, not federal micromanagement, should determine curricula, and that parents should be able to choose between public, private or home education.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations for the 2025-2026 term, chairing the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration subcommittee.
Elected Chairman of the House Freedom Caucus on September 17, 2024.

candidates.name: Dan Schwartz
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 46.3% of the vote.

summary.text: Dan Schwartz is the Democratic nominee for Maryland's 1st Congressional District and a first-time candidate for office. He spent more than a decade working on consumer financial protection at the Conference of State Bank Supervisors before leaving to run. He describes his campaign as focused on affordability, the economy, representation and election reform.

background.text: Born in New York, New York, and graduated from Hall High School.
Earned a bachelor's degree from George Washington University in 2010.

Worked for the Conference of State Bank Supervisors in Washington, D.C. for more than a decade, most recently as a senior director, in consumer financial protection; he describes his career as working with state and federal regulators to protect consumers from financial misconduct. He left the job in April 2025 to run for Congress.

A resident of Talbot County and described as a political newcomer, he won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 46.3% of the vote over Randi White and others, and was endorsed by Gov. Wes Moore and Sen. Chris Van Hollen among others.

priorities.text: Affordability and the economy, saying he will fight policies like spending freezes and tariffs that he says make it harder for families to save and businesses to plan.
Protecting and improving access to affordable health care and public health research funding he says has been cut by the Trump administration and DOGE.
Investing in Maryland's environment and future so working families can stay in the state.

positions.summary: Says he will fight tariff policies that he says make it impossible for families to save and small businesses to plan for the future.
positions.quote: I will fight dangerous policies like spending freezes and tariffs that make it impossible for families to save, and small businesses to plan for the future.

positions.summary: Says he will improve and protect access to affordable health care and support public health research funding.

researchNotes: Dan Schwartz's campaign website was not located; his biography draws on Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey and news reports.
